newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude physical softer, forward markets slow.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude physical softer, forward markets slow.

text.p: A cargo of August 18-20 Brent crude traded on Tuesday at September Brent +18 cents, the equivalent of a 10 cent drop from a deal on Friday, traders said.
Three Brent August 20-22 cargoes are expected to pass through the paper chains on Tuesday. This includes one deferred following a clocking on Monday.

Traders said the markets were quiet with potential buyers holding back for further news from Iraq. "I don't think news that Iraqi crude would be on the water soon would feed directly into the North Sea sweet crudes but it would trickle through and turn sentiment so people are holding off," one trader said.
Brent Aug/Sep lost ground after deals late Monday at +30 and +31 cents the market moved back down to trade on Tuesday at +25 cents. Brokers saw best bid at +23 cents.

The CFD market was relatively quiet with only two deals reported - an August 23-29 at October -14 cents and an August 11-18 versus August 21-29 at +9 cents. Levels eased back in thin talk after the physical Brent deal was reported.
Nigerian crude eased as late August loading cargoes struggled to find homes in the U.S. Gulf, traders said.
"Very little has moved in the last few days," said a trader.
With Asian demand covered, about 10 million barrels of sweet crude were still available this month, most offered on a delivered basis to U.S. buyers.
Dealing was also subdued as equity holders awaited the release of September loading schedules due this week.
Bonny Light was pegged a couple of cents lower at around Dated Brent +45 cents. Forcados was also seen softer at about Dated Brent +30 cents.
August loadings of Oso condensate were delayed by up to 14 days after field operator Mobil shut down production early last week following a technical failure.

Traders said a Mobil cargo due to load last weekend had been delayed to August 16th and two cargoes belonging to NNPC, Mobil's Oso joint venture partner, and a further Mobil cargo were subject to similar delays.
Mobil said it planned to restart Oso production on Tuesday, reaching the normal 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) level "in a few days".
